subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Exoskeleton
novels.author: Shane Stadler (2012)
novels.vibe: A sci-fi-horror prison novel about a convict who trades a 25-year sentence for a year of experimental, body-warping torment.
novels.summary: Facing 25 years behind bars, a convict instead volunteers for an experimental corrections program, believing it's his best shot at redemption. What follows is an escalating series of physical and psychological trials that transform him into something no longer entirely human.
novels.warnings: Extreme graphic torture (including dental/bone-related content), body horror, psychological abuse, confinement.

novels.title: The Troop
novels.author: Nick Cutter (2014)
novels.vibe: Lord of the Flies with parasitic worms and no safety rails.
novels.summary: A scoutmaster takes a small troop of boys on a routine camping trip to a remote Canadian island, only to have a starving, infected stranger stagger into camp. Once the parasite spreads, the story turns into a brutally graphic survival nightmare as hunger, infection, and cruelty strip away any veneer of civility.
novels.warnings: Extreme gore, body horror, animal death, starvation, bullying, child endangerment.

novels.title: The Vegetarian
novels.author: Han Kang (2007, tr. 2015)
novels.vibe: A literary, three-part Korean novel where a woman's quiet decision to stop eating meat spirals into total bodily and psychic transformation.
novels.summary: After a disturbing dream, Yeong-hye renounces meat entirely, a choice her husband and family meet with escalating incomprehension, control, and violence. Told across three shifting perspectives, the novel follows her withdrawal from her own body and eventual desire to become something else — plant, not person.
novels.warnings: Sexual violence, force-feeding, self-harm, domestic and family violence, disordered eating, psychiatric institutionalization.

novels.title: The Cipher
novels.author: Kathe Koja (1991 / 2020 ed.)
novels.vibe: Grimy, intimate 90s body horror about two awful people and the hole that eats them.
novels.summary: Nicholas and his girlfriend Nakota discover a strange, pulsing black hole—“the Funhole”—in a storage room and start experimenting on it, filming what happens when they put things inside. As the hole reacts in unsettling, flesh‑adjacent ways and Nicholas’s body begins to change, the book becomes a claustrophobic spiral of obsession, abuse, and physical transformation.
novels.warnings: Extreme body horror, self-harm, addiction, emotional abuse, obsession, misogyny, graphic violence.

short_works.title: Skeleton
short_works.author: Ray Bradbury (1943)
short_works.vibe: Classic weird‑tale body horror about a man and the skeleton he can’t stop thinking about.
short_works.summary: Mr. Harris becomes obsessed with the idea that his skeleton is a separate, hostile presence inside him and seeks help after his regular doctor dismisses him. The “specialist” he finds takes a far too literal interest in Harris’s bones, leading to a quietly grotesque finale that makes everyday anatomy feel uncanny.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, medical manipulation, obsession, unsettling doctor–patient dynamics.

short_works.title: The Body Politic
short_works.author: Clive Barker (1984)
short_works.vibe: A gleefully absurd body-horror revolt story where a man's own hands decide they'd rather not be attached to him anymore.
short_works.summary: Charlie's hands have started to feel like they don't belong to the rest of him, and it turns out they agree — plotting, along with hands everywhere, to free themselves from human bodies entirely. What starts as a strange domestic unease escalates into a citywide uprising of body parts against the people they're attached to.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, dismemberment, graphic violence, disturbing/surreal imagery.

short_works.title: What Moves the Dead
short_works.author: T. Kingfisher (2022)
short_works.vibe: A fungal, atmospheric reimagining of Poe's Fall of the House of Usher, heavy on decay and body horror.
short_works.summary: A former soldier arrives at the crumbling Usher estate to see an old friend through a mysterious wasting illness, only to find the surrounding land — and the house itself — thick with an unsettling fungal presence. As the sickness and the fungus intertwine, the story builds toward a genuinely unnerving, body-horror-inflected explanation for the Usher family's decline.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, decomposition/gore, suicide, animal death, possession, discriminatory language (period-typical), guns.

short_works.title: Who Goes There?
short_works.author: John W. Campbell Jr. (1938)
short_works.vibe: The Antarctic shape-shifting-alien novella that became The Thing — paranoia and body horror in a frozen research base.
short_works.summary: An Antarctic research team thaws out the frozen body of a crashed alien, only to discover it can perfectly imitate and replace any living thing it consumes. As the crew realizes anyone among them could already be the creature in disguise, the story becomes a claustrophobic, body-horror-driven exercise in paranoia.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, graphic violence, identity/body-snatching themes, period-typical racial homogeneity in characterization.
